messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the oscillating system. System velocity is the key kinematic variable that determines the magnitude of this resistive force. Force magnitude also depends on the damping coefficient of the surrounding medium. Medium viscosity and density are the physical properties that determine the damping coefficient. Coefficient values can be determined experimentally or calculated from fluid dynamics. Dynamics of the physical pendulum must include this term when the pendulum swings through a fluid. Fluid resistance is negligible for heavy, compact pendulums in air but critical for small or light ones. Ones that experience large relative damping require the viscous friction term in the equation of motion. Motion becomes overdamped or underdamped depending on the ratio of damping to the natural frequency. Frequency of oscillation is affected by the presence of viscous friction, slightly lowering the oscillation rate.
